reason: Which WWR model suits abrupt exposure jumps: the jump approach, matched against hazard rate, structural and parametric features.
Margin is near useless when exposure jumps at default, which the jump approach shows; continuous approaches show margin effective.
Characterises the jump approach against the hazard rate, structural and parametric descriptions.
Why CCPs are prone to WWR: defaulter-pays resources insufficient, losses pushed to surviving members and the CCP.
CCP initial margin and default fund follow market risk and ignore WWR, which rises with credit quality.
CCP WWR from adverse selection of margin assets relative to haircut; a CCP WWR effect in the source notes.
Allocating market, liquidity and operational risk between margin giver and receiver; no A20 selector.
Plain unilateral CVA calculation with no wrong-way risk; belongs to CVA, not A20.
WWR reduces the benefit of collateral, jumps in the margin period, systemic dealers; margin does not remove WWR.
Buying CDS protection on own sovereign from a domestic bank is WWR, and margin helps little against a jump.
A bank posting its own sovereign's bonds is wrong-way collateral, a weaker but not worthless mitigant.
Cross-currency swap: margin in the currency being paid is wrong-way collateral.
Identifying wrong-way collateral: even euro cash posted by a European bank can be wrong-way.
Classifying wrong-way margin as general or specific: own-sovereign bonds, payer versus receiver swap with government bonds.
CCP waterfall as a CDO: surviving members' default fund is a senior second-loss tranche exposed in systemic WWR scenarios.
Channels through which WWR strains CCP resources: margin driven by market risk, adverse selection, credit quality; netting claim is false.
Hazard rate approach gives only weak dependence even at high correlation and may underestimate WWR.
Structural approach with bivariate copula: opaque correlation and unconditional exposure information as the drawbacks.
Hull and White parametric approach: calibration reliable only if current portfolio resembles the historical one.
CVA versus FVA under a two-way CSA and the margin period of risk; no WWR selector.
Independence assumption behind the standard CVA formula; a CVA-mechanics point, not the WWR test itself.
CVA calculation under different credit curve shapes with no wrong-way risk; no A20 selector.
Margin does not remove WWR at a CCP: jumps, margin period volatility and systemic margin posters.
CDSs are hard to clear because a member's default is adversely linked to CDS values, so CCPs are prone to WWR.
Clearing does not eliminate WWR: unmatched book at default, losses beyond defaulter resources fall on surviving members.
Credit view of CCR leaves CVA changes unmanaged; no WWR selector.
Stress test of exposure-default correlation in CVA; CVA stress testing, not a WWR selector.
Economic capital aggregation of market and credit risk; mentions wrong-way risk only in passing.
